court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Saharanpur in Original Suit No. 323 of 2022
case_name: Smt Anchal Goyal vs Parag Goyal
facts_of_case: The wife filed an amendment application to introduce two paragraphs as paragraph nos. 54(cid:128) and 54(cid:129), to her written statement. The trial court dismissed the application.

legal_principles.principle: An order allowing or disallowing an application to amend a pleading will be a case decided and revisable if the amendment sought has a direct bearing on the rights of the parties and affects their obligations.
legal_principles.held: The key to the solution in determining whether an order allowing or disallowing an application for amendment of a pleading will be a case decided is to be sought in the nature of the amendment sought, its direct or likely impact on the rights and obligations of the parties concerned and its immediate or potential effect on the Court's jurisdiction.
cited_cases: Shankerlal Aggarwal and Others Vs. Shankerlal Poddar and Others, AIR 1965 SC 507
The Central Bank of India Ltd. v. Gokul Chand AIR 1967 SC 79 at 800

legal_principles.principle: An order passed under Order VI, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, either allowing an amendment or refusing to allow an amendment, is a 'case decided' within the meaning of that expression in Section 115, Code of Civil Procedure.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order VI, Rule 17

outcome.final_order: The amendment application filed by the wife was dismissed by the trial court, which decision is upheld on appeal.
